statement: Ana cuts a rectangle of brownies with 2 straight cuts from the left edge to the right edge and 3 from the top edge to the bottom edge. How many pieces are there?

choices.misconception: I added the number of cuts, 2 + 3.
I multiplied the number of cuts, 2 times 3, instead of the number of strips.
I added the 3 rows and the 4 columns instead of multiplying them.
I counted a strip on each side of every cut, which made 4 rows and 5 columns.

hints: How many rows do the 2 side-to-side cuts make?
Draw it. Cuts that go across split the tray into rows, and cuts that go down split it into columns. Count the rows and the columns, then count the pieces in the grid.
The 2 cuts across make 3 rows. The 3 cuts down make 4 columns. Every row is split into 4 pieces.

solutions.reliable: Two cuts from left to right split the brownies into 3 rows. Three cuts from top to bottom split them into 4 columns. Each of the 3 rows has 4 pieces, so there are $3 \times 4 = 12$ pieces. The idea to keep: a strip has one more piece than it has cuts, so draw the cuts and count the pieces.

whyOnTest: It checks the one-more rule for cuts and strips, and drawing the grid beats juggling the numbers of cuts.
